origin.description: Coerce through as.zoo, then attach a frequency.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object that as.zoo can convert.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Passed to as.zooreg after the zoo exists, not to as.zoo.
Passed to as.zoo, not to the frequency assignment.

origin.details: The body is as.zooreg(as.zoo(x, ...), frequency = frequency). A numeric vector therefore becomes a zoo with index 1, 2, ..., and that index is then tested for regularity. Equally spaced integer indexes get frequency 1. An explicit frequency is assigned onto that zoo and does not rebuild the index as yearqtr or yearmon.
origin.example:
x <- as.zooreg.default(1:5)
cat(paste(coredata(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(paste(index(x), collapse = " "), "\n", sep = "")
cat(frequency(x), "\n", sep = "")

translation.description: Coerce through as_zoo, then attach a frequency.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: An object as_zoo accepts. Extra keywords are passed to as_zoo.

arguments.name: frequency
arguments.text: Assigned after the zoo is built. None asks the index for a frequency.

translation.details: as_zooreg_default calls as_zoo, then as_zooreg. A 1-based integer index is regular with frequency 1. frequency=4 on that index stores 4 and leaves the index numeric; it does not call the yearqtr conversion that zoo uses at construction.
translation.example:
from zoo.as_zoo import as_zooreg_default
import numpy as np
x = as_zooreg_default(np.arange(1, 6))
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.asarray(x.data).reshape(-1)))
print(" ".join(str(int(v)) for v in np.asarray(x.index).reshape(-1)))
print(int(x.frequency))
